Name: Aloevera
Description: A succulent plant species known for its medicinal properties. It is cultivated worldwide for its gel, which is used in various health and beauty products.
Location: Found in tropical climates, commonly grown in gardens and as potted plants indoors.
Medical_Usage: Used for treating skin conditions, burns, wounds, and as a dietary supplement.

Name: Amla
Description: A deciduous tree native to the Indian subcontinent, known for its small, greenish-yellow fruits rich in vitamin C and antioxidants.
Location: Commonly found in deciduous forests and cultivated across India, including states like Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
Medical_Usage: Utilized in traditional medicine for its antioxidant properties; used to treat conditions like diabetes, inflammation, and digestive disorders.

Name: Amruta_Balli
Description: A large climbing shrub known for its heart-shaped leaves and medicinal properties, commonly referred to as Giloy in Hindi.
Location: Widely distributed throughout tropical regions of India, including dry and deciduous forests.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine to boost immunity, treat fevers, and manage diabetes; known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

Name: Arali
Description: A flowering plant known for its ornamental value and fragrant flowers, commonly referred to as Oleander.
Location: Native to the Mediterranean region and widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical areas.
Medical_Usage: Despite its toxicity, it has been used in traditional medicine for heart conditions and as a diuretic; however, caution is advised due to its poisonous nature.

Name: Ashoka
Description: A rain-forest tree known for its beautiful foliage and fragrant flowers, revered in Indian culture and mythology.
Location: Found in the Indian subcontinent, particularly in the Himalayas, Kerala, and Bengal regions.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine for gynecological disorders, pain relief, and as a uterine tonic.

Name: Ashwagandha
Description: A small shrub with yellow flowers, known as Indian ginseng or winter cherry, valued for its adaptogenic properties.
Location: Native to India and North Africa; thrives in dry regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to reduce stress, improve concentration, and increase energy levels; also employed in managing anxiety and boosting fertility.

Name: Avacado
Description: A tropical tree known for its nutrient-rich, creamy fruits.
Location: Native to Central and South America; cultivated in tropical and Mediterranean climates worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Rich in healthy fats, vitamins, and minerals; supports heart health, aids digestion, and has anti-inflammatory properties.

Name: Bamboo
Description: A fast-growing grass species known for its tall, woody stems and versatility.
Location: Found in diverse climates, from tropical to temperate regions, particularly in Asia.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine for its anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties; young shoots are edible and nutritious.

Name: Basale
Description: A fast-growing, soft-stemmed vine known for its succulent leaves, commonly referred to as Malabar spinach.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia; thrives in tropical and subtropical climates.
Medical_Usage: Leaves are rich in vitamins A and C, iron, and calcium; used to treat diarrhea and as a laxative; promotes eye health.

Name: Betel
Description: A vine whose leaves are commonly chewed in South and Southeast Asia for their stimulant effects.
Location: Cultivated in tropical climates, particularly in India, Sri Lanka, and Indonesia.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine as a breath freshener, digestive aid, and for its antiseptic properties.

Name: Betel_Nut
Description: The seed of the Areca palm, commonly chewed with betel leaves as a stimulant.
Location: Grown in tropical Pacific, Asia, and parts of east Africa.
Medical_Usage: Used traditionally to stimulate digestion and as a mild stimulant; however, it poses significant health risks including cancer.

Name: Brahmi
Description: A creeping herb known for its small leaves and purple flowers, valued in Ayurvedic medicine.
Location: Found in wet, tropical environments, particularly in India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and China.
Medical_Usage: Used to enhance cognitive function, improve memory, and reduce anxiety; also applied for its antioxidant properties.

Name: Castor
Description: A fast-growing shrub known for its large, glossy leaves and oil-rich seeds.
Location: Native to the southeastern Mediterranean Basin, Eastern Africa, and India; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Castor oil extracted from seeds is used as a laxative, in skin care, and for its anti-inflammatory properties.

Name: Curry_Leaf
Description: A small tree whose aromatic leaves are used as a flavoring agent in Indian cuisine.
Location: Native to India and Sri Lanka; commonly grown in home gardens.
Medical_Usage: Leaves are used to aid digestion, manage diabetes, and have antioxidant properties.

Name: Doddapatre
Description: A fleshy, aromatic herb known for its medicinal properties, commonly referred to as Indian borage.
Location: Grows in tropical and subtropical regions; commonly found in India.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat coughs, colds, and digestive issues; has antimicrobial properties.

Name: Ekka
Description: A traditional medicinal plant also known as Crown flower or Calotropis gigantea, noted for its white or lavender flowers.
Location: Grows wild in dry regions of India and Southeast Asia.
Medical_Usage: Used traditionally for treating joint pain, skin diseases, and respiratory ailments; also has anti-inflammatory properties.

Name: Ganike
Description: Known as Garcinia indica or Kokum, a tropical fruit-bearing tree with culinary and medicinal uses.
Location: Native to the Western Ghats region of India, especially in Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat acidity, heat strokes, and digestion issues; the rind is used in syrups and juices.

Name: Gauva
Description: A tropical fruit known for its sweet flavor and medicinal benefits.
Location: Cultivated widely in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in India and Southeast Asia.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat diarrhea, diabetes, and cough; rich in vitamin C and antioxidants.

Name: Geranium
Description: A group of flowering plants known for their fragrance and ornamental value.
Location: Native to temperate regions; commonly cultivated as ornamental plants worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Used in aromatherapy and herbal remedies to relieve stress, inflammation, and skin irritations.

Name: Henna
Description: A flowering plant used to make dye for coloring hair, skin, and fabrics.
Location: Native to North Africa, Asia, and northern Australia.
Medical_Usage: Used for its cooling and antimicrobial effects; treats headaches, skin conditions, and fevers.

Name: Hibiscus
Description: A genus of flowering plants known for large, colorful blossoms.
Location: Grows in warm-temperate, subtropical and tropical regions throughout the world.
Medical_Usage: Used to lower blood pressure, improve liver health, and promote hair growth.

Name: Honge
Description: Known as Indian Beech or Pongamia, a tree valued for its oil-producing seeds.
Location: Common in India, especially in dry regions.
Medical_Usage: Used for skin diseases, wounds, and as an anti-inflammatory; oil is used in Ayurvedic preparations.

Name: Insulin
Description: Commonly refers to the Insulin Plant (Costus igneus), known for its anti-diabetic properties.
Location: Grown in gardens in tropical climates, particularly in South India.
Medical_Usage: Used to help regulate blood sugar levels naturally; leaves are consumed directly.

Name: Jasmine
Description: A fragrant flowering plant widely used in perfumes and traditional medicine.
Location: Native to tropical and warm temperate regions of Eurasia and Oceania.
Medical_Usage: Used to reduce anxiety, improve mood, and promote restful sleep; also used in skin treatments.

Name: Lemon
Description: A small evergreen tree producing citrus fruits rich in vitamin C.
Location: Cultivated in tropical and subtropical climates around the world.
Medical_Usage: Boosts immunity, aids digestion, and has detoxifying properties.

Name: Lemon_grass
Description: A tropical plant known for its citrus scent and culinary uses.
Location: Commonly grown in Southeast Asia and India.
Medical_Usage: Used to relieve anxiety, improve digestion, and reduce cholesterol; often brewed as tea.

Name: Mango
Description: A tropical fruit-bearing tree highly prized for its sweet, juicy fruit.
Location: Widely grown in India, Southeast Asia, and tropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Rich in vitamins; aids digestion, supports immunity, and promotes eye health.

Name: Mint
Description: A fragrant herb widely used in cooking and traditional medicine.
Location: Grows easily in moist areas; cultivated worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Aids digestion, relieves nausea and headaches, and has a cooling effect.

Name: Nagadali
Description: Known in some regions as Clerodendrum serratum, traditionally used in Ayurveda.
Location: Native to India and Southeast Asia; found in forest regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat respiratory issues like asthma and bronchitis, and as an anti-inflammatory.

Name: Neem
Description: A fast-growing tree known for its medicinal properties and bitter leaves.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent; thrives in tropical and semi-tropical climates.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat skin conditions, dental problems, and as a natural insecticide.

Name: Nithyapushpa
Description: Commonly known as Periwinkle (Catharanthus roseus), a flowering plant with medicinal uses.
Location: Native to Madagascar but widely cultivated in India and other tropical areas.
Medical_Usage: Used in cancer treatment (vincristine, vinblastine) and for diabetes in traditional medicine.

Name: Nooni
Description: Commonly known as Noni (Morinda citrifolia), a tropical fruit-bearing tree.
Location: Found in Southeast Asia, Pacific Islands, and India.
Medical_Usage: Used to boost immunity, relieve pain, and reduce inflammation; often consumed as juice.

Name: Pappaya
Description: A tropical tree producing soft, sweet fruits rich in enzymes and vitamins.
Location: Native to Central America; widely grown in India and tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to improve digestion, reduce inflammation, and aid in skin care.

Name: Pepper
Description: A flowering vine known for its spicy fruit, commonly used as a seasoning.
Location: Native to South India; cultivated in tropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Stimulates digestion, relieves cold symptoms, and has antimicrobial properties.

Name: Pomegranate
Description: A fruit-bearing deciduous shrub known for its red, juicy seeds.
Location: Cultivated in the Mediterranean region, Middle East, and India.
Medical_Usage: Rich in antioxidants; supports heart health, reduces inflammation, and may prevent cancer.

Name: Raktachandini
Description: Also known as Red Sandalwood (Pterocarpus santalinus), used in traditional medicine.
Location: Native to India, especially Andhra Pradesh.
Medical_Usage: Used for treating skin diseases, wounds, and as an anti-inflammatory agent.

Name: Rose
Description: A widely cultivated ornamental flower known for its fragrance and beauty.
Location: Grown globally; thrives in temperate and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Rose petals and oil are used for skin care, stress relief, and digestive health.

Name: Sapota
Description: Also known as Chikoo, a tropical fruit with sweet, grainy pulp.
Location: Native to Mexico and Central America; widely grown in India.
Medical_Usage: Improves digestion, boosts immunity, and has anti-inflammatory properties.

Name: Tulasi
Description: Also called Holy Basil, a sacred plant in Indian culture with medicinal benefits.
Location: Widely cultivated in Indian households and temples.
Medical_Usage: Used for respiratory disorders, stress relief, and boosting immunity.

Name: Wood_sorel
Description: A small herbaceous plant with sour-tasting leaves, commonly known as Indian sorrel.
Location: Found in moist, shady areas across India and tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used for treating fever, urinary infections, and as an appetite stimulant.
